canonical_statement: The study objective was to describe trends in the incidence of invasive MRSA infections in children during 2005-2010.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To describe trends in the incidence of invasive methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infections in children during 2005–2010.

canonical_statement: ABCs invasive MRSA surveillance covered selected counties in 9 geographically diverse US metropolitan areas and approximately 4.4 million persons younger than 18 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: selected counties in 9 geographically diverse metropolitan areas with a population of ~4.4 million persons younger than 18 years

population.label: ABCs surveillance population: persons <18 years in selected counties across 9 US metropolitan areas

canonical_statement: An invasive MRSA case required MRSA isolation from a normally sterile body site in a surveillance-area resident younger than 18 years, with recurrent qualifying cultures separated by at least 30 days.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A case of invasive MRSA infection was defined by the isolation of MRSA from a normally sterile body site

population.label: Eligible invasive MRSA cases in surveillance-area residents <18 years
inclusion_criteria: MRSA isolated from a normally sterile body site
exclusion_criteria: Subsequent qualifying cultures <30 days from an initial invasive MRSA culture

canonical_statement: Invasive MRSA infection was defined by isolation of MRSA from a normally sterile body site.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: isolation of MRSA from a normally sterile body site

outcome.definition: MRSA isolated from a normally sterile body site

canonical_statement: Surveillance personnel abstracted demographics, clinical characteristics, outcomes, and established health care risk factors from medical records.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Demographic characteristics, clinical characteristics, disease outcomes, and information on established health care risk factors were abstracted from medical records.

canonical_statement: Hospital-onset (HO) cases had the MRSA culture collected on or after hospital day 4.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cases were considered hospital-onset (HO) if the MRSA clinical culture was obtained on or after the fourth calendar day of hospitalization

canonical_statement: Health care-associated community-onset (HACO) cases had the culture collected as an outpatient or before hospital day 4 in a patient with an established health care risk factor.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: as health care–associated community-onset (HACO) if the culture was obtained in an outpatient setting or before the fourth calendar day

canonical_statement: Community-associated (CA) cases had the culture collected as an outpatient or before hospital day 4 without a documented health care risk factor.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: as CA if the culture was obtained in an outpatient setting or before the fourth calendar day of hospitalization

canonical_statement: For young infants, early-onset infection was defined as MRSA isolation before 3 days of age and late-onset infection as 3-89 days of age.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: early-onset infection if MRSA was isolated from infants younger than 3 days or late-onset infection if infants were 3 to 89 days

canonical_statement: A convenience sample of MRSA isolates was submitted to CDC for confirmation, susceptibility testing, and molecular characterization including PFGE; from 2008, PFGE patterns could also be inferred from microbiologic characteristics.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a convenience sample of MRSA isolates is sent to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) for further testing

canonical_statement: Incidence used Census bridged-race population estimates; unknown race was imputed by local known race and gender distributions, and the population younger than 90 days was approximated as one-quarter of infants younger than 1 year.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Because there are no population estimates for infants by month of age, we estimated that the population of infants younger than 90 days was approximately one-quarter

canonical_statement: Incidence trends were modeled with Poisson regression or negative binomial models when overdispersion was present, using year as a continuous predictor and adjusting trend models for age, gender, and race.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Trends in incidence were assessed by using a Poisson regression model or negative binomial distribution, if there was evidence of overdispersion.

canonical_statement: National 2010 burden estimates applied surveillance-site age- and race-specific incidence to the US population, with confidence intervals based on the gamma distribution.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For national estimates of cases in 2010, age- and race-specific incidence of infection across surveillance sites were applied to the age and racial distribution of the US population.

canonical_statement: During 2005-2010, 876 invasive MRSA cases were identified among 834 pediatric patients; median age was 2.1 years and 39% of cases occurred in infants younger than 1 year.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: During 2005 through 2010, 876 cases of invasive MRSA infections were reported among 834 pediatric patients.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that invasive MRSA infection in children disproportionately affected young infants and Black children.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that no significant reductions in invasive health care-associated MRSA infections occurred in children older than 3 months during 2005-2010, while invasive CA-MRSA incidence increased.

canonical_statement: The authors stated that optimal pediatric MRSA prevention strategies remained to be defined, particularly for children without health care risk factors and for health care-exposed children outside intensive care.
